top_choice_rationale: P001 (Helpman and Melitz, B001) rewards one identifiable, mature discovery. Melitz (2003) and Helpman, Melitz and Yeaple (2004) showed that firms differing in productivity select into exporting, foreign investment or neither. This made reallocation across firms a channel for the gains from trade and produced predictions that more than twenty years of firm-level data have tested and refined. The framework is also widely used in macro, growth and productivity work. The main risk is attribution: Bernard, Eaton, Jensen and Kortum (2003) is a close contemporaneous heterogeneous-producer model, and the exporter-premia facts and Redding's quantitative work are not credited here. I judge this manageable only if the citation is confined to selection into exporting and foreign investment and to reallocation across firms, makes no claim about welfare magnitudes, and the scientific background acknowledges the parallel work. The exports-versus-FDI sorting result has no counterpart in that parallel work, as I read it. I rank no award last because the pair's contribution is substantial enough that awarding it is better than awarding nothing. No other proposal is on the slate. The apparent unanimity of the round-2 files is not independent evidence, since they share one model and similar reasoning.
recusal_note: No tie to Helpman or Melitz is apparent from the profile. I disclose thematic proximity: my research on creative destruction, misallocation and structural change is adjacent to the reallocation literature that P001's framework fed, which could bias me toward it. I have a long-running collaboration with Peter Klenow, credited in B050, which is not on the slate. I also co-author frequently with Per Krusell (secretary) and have co-authored with John Hassler (chair). I co-wrote the Ekonomisk Debatt summaries of the 2024 and 2025 prizes, and the 2025 Scientific Background cites my work. I disclose these and do not adjudicate them.
